Panevezys Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Demolished. Panevėžys — Lithuania's fifth-largest city — became known, after Telšiai, as the second stronghold of Orthodox Jewry in the country, its fame as a Torah study center spreading worldwide; the yeshiva founded here by Rabbi Yitzhak Yaakov Rabinovich in 1908 became one of the greatest in Lithuania, and after his successor Rabbi Yosef-Shlomo Kahaneman re-established it in Bnei Brak, Israel, in 1944, it grew into one of the leading Litvish yeshivas in Israel today — the original prewar building still stands in the city center, marked by a plaque. The Jewish population reached 6,627 (51 percent of the town) by 1897, and a Star of David — an unusually explicit Jewish symbol for a Soviet-era monument — was placed on the postwar memorial at the mass graves in Pajuoste forest, where the community was annihilated between August 24 and 26, 1941. This cemetery, opened in the 18th century and later expanded twice, was formally closed in 1955 and liquidated by city officials in 1966, who built a park with a central fountain on the site; headstones were used for construction around the city, including in a decorative wall at the Drama Theatre. A statue, 'The Grieving Jewish Mother,' was unveiled by the recreated Panevėžys Jewish Community in 2009.
